extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX/TikZ users creating diagrams (matrices, mindmaps, Petri nets, patterns)
extracted.subtask_description: Usage and style guidelines for TikZ matrix delimiters, the mindmap drawing library (concept nodes, connections, color transitions, annotations) and the Petri-net drawing library (places, transitions, tokens, token placement). Includes pattern-filling notes and implementation/workarounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiters — general behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Delimiters are parentheses or braces to the left and right of a formula or a matrix; the matrix library offers options for adding such delimiters to a matrix, but delimiters can be added to any node that has the standard anchors (north, south, north west, etc.). They are implemented by measuring the height of the node and then adding a delimiter of the correct size to the left or right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use delimiters on any node with standard anchors; they work by sizing to the node's height so they can be applied to matrices and rectangle boxes alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: left delimiter=(delimiter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option to add a left delimiter to any node that has the standard anchors; the delimiter can be any delimiter acceptable to TeX's \left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use e.g. left delimiter=( and pair with right delimiter=\} for matrices or nodes. Works on any node with anchors.

rubrics_metrics.name: right delimiter=(delimiter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option to add a right delimiter to any node that has the standard anchors; the delimiter can be any delimiter acceptable to TeX's \right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair with left delimiter as needed; both delimiters size themselves to the node height.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every delimiter
rubrics_metrics.description: A style executed for every delimiter; used to shift, color, or otherwise modify delimiters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to change visual attributes of all delimiters globally (e.g., color or xshift).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every left delimiter
rubrics_metrics.description: A style executed for every left delimiter (in addition to style=every delimiter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for left-delimiter-specific adjustments (e.g., move left delimiters inward via xshift).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every right delimiter
rubrics_metrics.description: A style executed for every right delimiter (in addition to style=every delimiter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for right-delimiter-specific adjustments (e.g., nudge right delimiters via xshift).

rubrics_metrics.name: above delimiter=(delimiter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option to add a delimiter above the node; implemented by rotating a left delimiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to place delimiters above a node; style=every above delimiter can be used for global control.

rubrics_metrics.name: below delimiter=(delimiter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option to add a delimiter below the node (works analogously to above delimiter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use together with style=every below delimiter for consistent below-delimiter formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every above delimiter
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed for every above delimiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to adjust the appearance or placement of all above delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every below delimiter
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed for every below delimiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to adjust the appearance or placement of all below delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the mindmap style for mindmap pictures/scopes
rubrics_metrics.description: style=mindmap installs internal settings useful for drawing mindmaps and should be used with pictures/scopes that contain a mindmap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrap mindmap content in a picture or scope with [mindmap] so default sizes, colors, and connection behavior are set up automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every mindmap
rubrics_metrics.description: A style included by the mindmap style that is executed for every mindmap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefine this style to add custom settings applied to all mindmaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=large mindmap
rubrics_metrics.description: A style that includes mindmap and changes default sizes/distances so a medium-size mindmap fits on A3 paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need a larger overall mindmap layout (A3). Large mindmap redefines level- and size-related styles; add adjustments inside the picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=huge mindmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Like large mindmap but for even bigger concepts (best used for A2 paper and above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for very large mindmaps; it increases default concept sizes and spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer building mindmaps using TikZ tree mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not strictly necessary, mindmaps are usually created using TikZ's tree mechanism; some styles/macros work best inside trees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use child/grow and tree-based constructs for natural layout and to take advantage of built-in level styles and edge-from-parent behavior. For parts that need arbitrary edges, treat them as graphs and add edges separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=concept for concept nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use style=concept with nodes that are concepts; this style makes the node circular and installs a uniform color called concept color and calls style=every concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concept for all concept nodes; rely on every concept to tweak text color and font. Keep concept fill/draw uniform for connection bar shading to work correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed for every concept; useful for changing appearance of concept nodes (text color/font) but should not change color/draw/fill state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change text-related appearance here. Avoid changing fill/draw/color here because the library expects uniform concept colors for smooth connection shading.

rubrics_metrics.name: concept color=(color)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option that tells TikZ which color should be used for filling and stroking concepts; it also lets TikZ track colors to create smooth shadings between connected concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set concept_color on nodes; when used on child operations TikZ will interpolate colors from parent to child automatically. Use consistent concept_color usage to enable smooth color transitions on connection bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=extra concept and style=every extra concept
rubrics_metrics.description: extra concept is for concepts not part of the mindmap tree but standing beside it (usually smaller and subdued); every extra concept changes appearance of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use extra concept to mark side annotations or secondary nodes; style them uniformly via every extra concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=root concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Style used for roots of mindmap trees; included by mindmap style; root-specific rendering should be added here (locally inside the picture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify root concept inside the picture (e.g., minimum size, concept color) to customize the root only for that picture; avoid global redefinition outside picture unless intended everywhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: level N concept styles (level 1..4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mindmap style adds level 1 concept, level 2 concept, level 3 concept, and level 4 concept styles for children at those depths; there are no built-in fifth+ level styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these styles to change appearance of children at different depths (e.g., color, size). For levels beyond 4 modify level 5 directly or add your own level styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child-level concept color transition
rubrics_metrics.description: When concept color is given as an option to the child operation (not the node or level style), TikZ will smoothly change the concept color from the parent's color to the child's color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get automatic shading transitions on parent→child edges, set concept_color on the child in the child[...] options rather than on the node itself or via the level style.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=concept connection
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended style for lines between two concepts to ensure consistent appearance; can be redefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define or customize concept connection to get consistent edge appearance across the mindmap. Use background layer if you draw connections after computing node coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place manually-drawn connections on background layer
rubrics_metrics.description: If connecting concepts after the main mindmap has been drawn you should place connecting lines on a background layer so they lie behind the main mindmap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw such lines inside \begin{pgfonlayer}{background} ... \end{pgfonlayer} to keep them behind nodes and other artwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circle connection bar snake parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: The circle connection bar snake is defined using macros; you must initialize \pgfsnakecirclestartradius and \pgfsnakecircleendradius and you can tweak \pgfsnakesegmentamplitude and \pgfsnakesegmentangle to influence shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set start/end radii and segment amplitude/angle to control the snake. The snake path starts at a border point on the first circle at the specified angle relative to the center-connecting line, becomes a rectangle of given thickness, and ends on the second circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill-only snake & circle size workaround for rounding errors
rubrics_metrics.description: When drawing the circle connection bar, fill the snake only (no stroke) and use the same color as the circles; make the circles slightly larger to cover rounding errors because TikZ/TeX have numerical limitations (e.g., square-root errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see small white gaps between the circle and the snake, increase circle size slightly (e.g., add 1pt) or set draw with an appropriate line width; set outer sep=0pt so snakes align with filled circle borders, not stroked borders.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=circle connection bar (to-path)
rubrics_metrics.description: A special to-path that performs computations for you: computes circle radii, sets internal snake macros, sets fill to concept color and draw=none, and uses the circle connection bar snake. Requires that start and target are named nodes of shape circle; otherwise it errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use node names and shape=circle when using to[circle connection bar]; if your nodes aren't circles or unnamed this to-path will produce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every circle connection bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Style included by circle connection bar; used to change appearance of circle connection bar to-paths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefine to customize fill/shading/other attributes of all circle-connection-bar to-paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: circle connection bar switch color=from ... to ...
rubrics_metrics.description: Works like circle connection bar but uses a shading between the from-color and the to-color instead of a single fill color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want the connection bar to visually transition from parent's concept color to child's color (creates smooth shading between two colors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multiple to operations with circle connection bar in one \path
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not advisable to have more than one to operation together with the circle connection bar option in a single \path; the to-path is complicated and expects single uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the edge operation instead for creating multiple connections — edge creates a new scope for each edge and avoids the multi-to pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mindmap tree edges use circle connection bar and color switching
rubrics_metrics.description: When a mindmap is built as a tree the mindmap option sets the edge from parent path to use circle connection bar (and circle connection bar switch color when concept_color changes), so parent→child edges automatically get shading and color transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on default tree-built edges for consistent connection appearance and automatic color transitions when using child[concept color=...].

rubrics_metrics.name: style=annotation and style=every annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: annotation style indicates that a node is an annotation node (some explanatory text outside the mindmap); every annotation customizes annotation appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use annotation/right/left placement together with every annotation to add explanatory text near concepts; typically used for comments or clarifications outside the mindmap itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the patterns library for area fills
rubrics_metrics.description: The patterns library provides patterns for filling areas (e.g., horizontal lines, vertical lines, north east lines, grid, crosshatch, dots, stars, bricks, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load via \usetikzlibrary{patterns} and choose pattern names to fill shapes; useful for distinguishing regions without color or for printing-friendly fills.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=place for Petri net places
rubrics_metrics.description: Use style=place to indicate a node is a place of a Petri net; places usually contain no text (use label to add text outside) and tokens should be added via the tokens options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep place node text empty, use label=above/below to name/annotate places and tokens/tokens options to show marking inside the place.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every place
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed for every place (invoked by place).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redefine every place to change default fill/draw/thickness/size of all places (e.g., minimum size, colors).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=transition and style=every transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use style=transition for transition nodes; like places, transitions normally have empty text and use label for names. style=every transition customizes all transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect transitions to places with edge and pre/post styles; set label=below:$t_1$ etc. Avoid putting text inside the transition node.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=pre, style=post, style=pre and post
rubrics_metrics.description: Styles for edges between transitions and places: pre indicates the place is in the pre-set, post indicates the post-set, and pre and post indicates both; defaults are provided (e.g., <-,shorten <=1pt for pre).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these styles on edges (edge[pre] or edge[post]) and redefine them if you need different arrowheads/shortening.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=token and style=every token
rubrics_metrics.description: Token nodes represent tokens; style=token defaults to a small black circle with optional text typeset tiny and white on black; every token lets you change token appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use token nodes for individual tokens when needed; change every token to alter defaults like size, color, font.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=children are tokens (token placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Places can use the children are tokens style to treat tokens as children placed using the tree growth mechanism; tokens are placed on top of the place with special mappings for up to nine tokens (arrangements for 1..9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use child { node[token] {...} } constructions under a place with [children are tokens] to let the library place 1..9 tokens automatically. For more than nine tokens you must implement custom placement code.

rubrics_metrics.name: token distance=(distance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the distance between centers of tokens in the arrangements provided by children are tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust token distance to increase/decrease spacing between tokens when using children are tokens mapping.
